questions.question: Which of the following functions is neither odd nor even?
questions.answer: $\tan x$ and $4x^5-x$ are odd functions ($f(-x)=-f(x)$) and $x^6$ is even ($f(-x)=f(x)$). For $e^x$, $e^{-x}\neq e^x$ and $e^{-x}\ne-e^x$, so it has neither line nor rotational symmetry: B.

questions.question:
A table of future values for an annuity of \$1 invested at the start of each period is shown.

| Periods | 1% | 2% | 3% | 4% | 5% | 6% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 5.1520 | 5.3081 | 5.4684 | 5.6330 | 5.8019 | 5.9753 |
| 10 | 10.5668 | 11.1687 | 11.8078 | 12.4864 | 13.2068 | 13.9716 |
| 15 | 16.2579 | 17.6393 | 19.1569 | 20.8245 | 22.6575 | 24.6725 |
| 20 | 22.2392 | 24.7833 | 27.6765 | 30.9692 | 34.7193 | 38.9927 |

Mark made equal instalments of \$550 twice per year for 10 years with each investment earning 6% p.a., compounded twice per year. The future value of this investment is:
questions.answer: Twice per year for 10 years gives $20$ periods at $6\%\div2=3\%$ per period. From the table, the future value factor is $27.6765$, so $FV=550\times27.6765=\$15\,222.08$.

questions.question:
The table shows the function values for $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$.

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | 3 | 0 | 3 | 12 | 27 |
| $g(x)$ | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 |

What is the value of $y=f\big(g(1)\big)$?

There are 73 teachers at a local school. Of these teachers: 11 teach Mathematics; 10 teach Science; 54 teach neither Mathematics nor Science. What is the probability that a teacher chosen at random teaches Mathematics only or Science only?
questions.answer: Teachers teaching Mathematics or Science: $73-54=19$. By inclusion–exclusion, those teaching both: $11+10-19=2$. Mathematics only $=9$, Science only $=8$, so $P=\dfrac{9+8}{73}=\dfrac{17}{73}$.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for $y=5\cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{3}\right)+1$?
questions.answer: Amplitude $=5$; period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi/3}=3$; the graph is shifted up by $1$, so the maximum is $5+1=6$ and the minimum is $-5+1=-4$.

questions.question: The random variable $X$ has a probability density function $y=f(x)$ as shown in the graph (defined from $x=1.7$ to $x=4.3$). What is the mode of the random variable $X$?
questions.answer: The mode is the $x$-value at which the probability density function is greatest. The graph has a local maximum of $0.4$ at $x=2.6$, but the greatest value of $f(x)$ is $0.6$, at the endpoint $x=4.3$. The mode is $x=4.3$.

questions.question: The function $f(x)=\dfrac1x$ has a restricted domain of $[a,b)$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers. The range of $f(x)=\dfrac1x$ is:
questions.answer: $f(x)=\frac1x$ is decreasing for $x>0$, so the largest value is at the left end, $f(a)=\frac1a$ (included, since $a$ is in the domain), and values approach $f(b)=\frac1b$ without reaching it (since $b$ is excluded). The range is $\left(\frac1b,\frac1a\right]$.

questions.question: For the function $y=h(x)$ it is given that $\displaystyle\int_a^bh(x)\,dx<0$. Which of the following MUST always be true?
options: All of the curve $y=h(x)$ is below the $x$-axis for $a\le x\le b$
The majority of the curve $y=h(x)$ is below the $x$-axis for $a\le x\le b$
The gradient of the curve $y=h(x)$ is negative for $a\le x\le b$
questions.answer: A negative definite integral means the signed area is negative, so the area below the $x$-axis exceeds the area above it (the net area is negative). So more of the area lies below the axis (C). The curve may still go above the axis in places (so B is not forced), the signs of $a,b$ are unrestricted, and nothing is implied about the gradient.

questions.question: The graph of $y=f'(x)$ is shown. Which of the following describes the graph of $y=f(x)$ at the point $x=-1$?
options: $x=-1$ is a horizontal point of inflexion
questions.answer: At $x=-1$ the graph of $f'(x)$ touches the $x$-axis (a local maximum of $f'$ with $f'(-1)=0$) and $f'(x)<0$ on both sides. So the gradient of $f$ is zero but does not change sign (it is negative before and after), and the concavity changes: a horizontal point of inflexion.

questions.question: The graphs of $f(x)=\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}2\right)$ and $g(x)=\sin(\pi x)$ are shown (they meet at $x=\tfrac13,\,1,\,\tfrac53$ and $3$). An integral expression that gives the total area of the shaded regions is:
questions.answer:
The upper curve changes at each intersection: from $0$ to $\tfrac13$, $f>g$ (area $=\int(f-g)$); from $\tfrac13$ to $1$, $g>f$ (area $=\int(g-f)=-\int(f-g)$); from $1$ to $\tfrac53$, $f>g$; from $\tfrac53$ to $3$, $g>f$ (area $=-\int(f-g)$). The graphs are symmetric under a half-turn about $(1,0)$, so the area from $1$ to $\tfrac53$ equals the area from $\tfrac13$ to $1$. So
$$\text{Area}=\int_0^{1/3}(f-g)\,dx-2\int_{1/3}^{1}(f-g)\,dx-\int_{5/3}^{3}(f-g)\,dx,$$
which is B. (In D the last integral should be $g-f$, not $f-g$.)

questions.question: Find the limiting sum of the series $96+72+54+\cdots$
questions.answer:
Geometric with $a=96$, $r=\dfrac{72}{96}=\dfrac34$, and $|r|<1$, so the limiting sum exists:
$$S_\infty=\frac a{1-r}=\frac{96}{1-\frac34}=384.$$

questions.question: Simplify $\dfrac{x^4-4x^2}{x^2-3x-10}$.
Solve the equation $\log_4(2x-1)-\log_4x=-1$.
questions.answer:
$$\log_4\frac{2x-1}x=-1\Rightarrow\frac{2x-1}x=4^{-1}=\frac14\Rightarrow8x-4=x\Rightarrow x=\frac47.$$
Check: $x=\tfrac47>\tfrac12$ so $2x-1>0$ and $x>0$, so the solution is valid.

questions.question: In the triangle shown (angles $48^\circ$ and $67^\circ$ as marked, the side $24$ cm between the $48^\circ$ angle and the third angle, and $x$ the side opposite the $48^\circ$ angle), find the length of $x$, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
By the sine rule ($x$ is opposite $48^\circ$ and $24$ is opposite $67^\circ$):
$$\frac x{\sin48^\circ}=\frac{24}{\sin67^\circ}\Rightarrow x=\frac{24\sin48^\circ}{\sin67^\circ}=19.38\text{ cm}.$$

questions.question: In the triangle shown, $x=19.38$ cm (found using the sine rule), the angles are $48^\circ$ and $67^\circ$ as marked, and the side opposite the $67^\circ$ angle is $24$ cm. Hence find the area of the triangle, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
The third angle is $180^\circ-48^\circ-67^\circ=65^\circ$, between the sides $24$ and $x$:
$$A=\tfrac12\times24\times19.38\times\sin65^\circ=210.77\text{ cm}^2.$$
(Using the unrounded $x=19.3758$ gives $210.72$ cm$^2$.)

questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int\left(\frac3{2x+1}+12x^3\right)dx$.
questions.answer: $$\int\frac3{2x+1}dx+\int12x^3dx=\frac32\ln|2x+1|+3x^4+C.$$

questions.question: Differentiate $y=\sqrt[3]{12x-11}$.
Differentiate $y=\dfrac{\cos(5x)}x$.
questions.answer:
Quotient rule with $u=\cos5x$, $u'=-5\sin5x$, $v=x$, $v'=1$:
$$y'=\frac{-5x\sin5x-\cos5x}{x^2}.$$

questions.question: An arithmetic series is $118+105+92+79+\cdots$. Find the 10th term of the series.
An arithmetic series is $118+105+92+79+\cdots$. Find the minimum number of terms needed for the sum of the series to be negative.
questions.answer:
$S_n=\dfrac n2\left[2(118)+(n-1)(-13)\right]=\dfrac n2(249-13n)<0$.

Since $n>0$, we need $249-13n<0\Rightarrow n>\dfrac{249}{13}=19.15\ldots$, so the minimum is $n=20$ terms. (Check: $S_{20}=10(249-260)=-110<0$ and $S_{19}=\tfrac{19}2(2)=19>0$.)

questions.question: Alyssa enters a catching competition where she attempts to take two catches. She either takes a catch (C) or drops a catch (D). The probability Alyssa takes the first catch is $0.93$. If she catches the first attempt, the probability she takes the second catch is $0.96$. If she drops the first attempt, the probability she takes the second catch is $0.81$. Complete the probability tree: give the probability on each branch.

Alyssa attempts two catches. The probability she takes the first catch is $0.93$. If she catches the first attempt, the probability she takes the second catch is $0.96$. If she drops the first attempt, the probability she takes the second catch is $0.81$. What is the probability that Alyssa takes both catches?

Alyssa attempts two catches. The probability she takes the first catch is $0.93$. If she catches the first attempt, the probability she takes the second catch is $0.96$. If she drops the first attempt, the probability she takes the second catch is $0.81$. Given that Alyssa takes at least one catch, find the probability that she takes both catches, as a decimal correct to 3 decimal places.
questions.answer:
$P(\text{at least one})=1-P(DD)=1-0.07\times0.19=0.9867$.
$$P(\text{both}\mid\text{at least one})=\frac{P(CC)}{P(\text{at least one})}=\frac{0.8928}{0.9867}=0.905\ (3\text{ d.p.}).$$

questions.question: Given that $\cos\theta=-\dfrac27$ and $\dfrac\pi2\le\theta\le\pi$, find the exact value of $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.
questions.answer:
$\theta$ is in the second quadrant, where $\sin\theta>0$. Using a right triangle with adjacent $2$ and hypotenuse $7$: opposite $=\sqrt{7^2-2^2}=\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt5$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac{3\sqrt5}7$.
$$\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\frac1{\sin\theta}=\frac7{3\sqrt5}=\frac{7\sqrt5}{15}.$$

questions.question: Given that $|t|=2$, find the values of $|t-3|-|1+3t|$.
Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{\ln2}\left(e^{2x}-6e^{3x}\right)dx$.
questions.answer: $$\left[\frac{e^{2x}}2-2e^{3x}\right]_0^{\ln2}=\left(\frac{e^{2\ln2}}2-2e^{3\ln2}\right)-\left(\frac12-2\right)=\left(\frac42-16\right)-\left(-\frac32\right)=-14+\frac32=-12.5.$$

questions.question: The graph of $y=\ln x$ is transformed to the graph $y=\ln\left(\dfrac1x\right)$. Describe the transformation.
questions.answer: $\ln\frac1x=\ln x^{-1}=-\ln x$. So the new graph is $y=-\ln x$, which is the graph of $y=\ln x$ **reflected in the $x$-axis**.

questions.question: The point $P$ on the graph $y=g(x)$ has coordinates $(-6,3)$. Find the coordinates of the image of point $P$ on the graph $y=g(2x-3)-4$.
questions.answer:
Write $y=g\big(2(x-\tfrac32)\big)-4$: the graph of $y=g(x)$ is dilated horizontally by a factor of $\tfrac12$ (so $x\to\tfrac x2$), translated $\tfrac32$ to the right, and translated $4$ down. Step by step: $(-6,3)\to(-3,3)\to\left(-\tfrac32,3\right)\to\left(-\tfrac32,-1\right)$.

(Check: the image point has $2x-3=-6\Rightarrow x=-\tfrac32$ and $y=g(-6)-4=3-4=-1$.)

The image of $P$ is $\left(-\tfrac32,-1\right)$.

questions.question: Prove that $$\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta+\sin\theta+\cos^2\theta}=1-\sin\theta.$$
questions.answer: $$\text{LHS}=\frac{\cos^2\theta}{(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)+\sin\theta}=\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\frac{1-\sin^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\frac{(1+\sin\theta)(1-\sin\theta)}{1+\sin\theta}=1-\sin\theta=\text{RHS}.$$

questions.question: Find the equation of the tangent, in simplest form, to the curve $y=x^2e^{-x}$ at $\left(1,\dfrac1e\right)$.
questions.answer:
Product rule: $y'=2xe^{-x}-x^2e^{-x}$. At $x=1$: $m=\dfrac2e-\dfrac1e=\dfrac1e$.

$$y-\frac1e=\frac1e(x-1)\Rightarrow y=\frac xe.$$

questions.question: Solve $3\sec\theta+4=0$ for $0\le\theta\le2\pi$, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
$\sec\theta=-\dfrac43\Rightarrow\cos\theta=-\dfrac34$. The related angle is $\cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac34\right)=0.7227\ldots$ rad. Cosine is negative in quadrants 2 and 3:

$\theta=\pi-0.7227=2.42$ or $\theta=\pi+0.7227=3.86$ (radians).

questions.question:
The probability distribution for the discrete random variable $X$ is shown below.

| $x$ | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X=x)$ | 0.35 | 0.44 | 0.1 | 0.11 |

Find $P(X>E(X))$.
When hot cooking oil cools down, its temperature $T$, in degrees Celsius, after $t$ minutes is given by $T=50+160e^{-0.1t}$. What is the initial temperature of the oil?

When hot cooking oil cools down, its temperature $T$, in degrees Celsius, after $t$ minutes is given by $T=50+160e^{-0.1t}$. Ricky is cooking and at that time the temperature is cooling at a rate of $10^\circ$C per minute. Calculate the temperature of the oil at that time.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-16e^{-0.1t}$. Cooling at $10^\circ$C per minute means $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-10$:
$$-16e^{-0.1t}=-10\Rightarrow e^{-0.1t}=\frac{10}{16}=0.625\Rightarrow t=-10\ln0.625=4.7\text{ min}.$$
$$T=50+160(0.625)=50+100=150^\circ\text{C}.$$

questions.question: When hot cooking oil cools down, its temperature $T$, in degrees Celsius, after $t$ minutes is given by $T=50+160e^{-0.1t}$. What temperature does the oil eventually cool to?
questions.answer: As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-0.1t}\to0$, so $T\to50^\circ$C.

questions.question: The curve $y=\sqrt x$ intersects the curve $y=\dfrac8x$ at $(4,2)$. The region bounded by the curve $y=\sqrt x$, the curve $y=\dfrac8x$, the line $x=8$ and the $x$-axis is shaded in the diagram. Find the area of the shaded region in simplest exact form.
questions.answer:
From $x=0$ to $4$ the region lies under $y=\sqrt x$; from $x=4$ to $8$ it lies under $y=\frac8x$:
$$A=\int_0^4x^{1/2}dx+\int_4^8\frac8x\,dx=\left[\frac{2x^{3/2}}3\right]_0^4+\Big[8\ln x\Big]_4^8=\frac{16}3+8\ln8-8\ln4=\frac{16}3+8\ln2\text{ square units}.$$

questions.question: A curve has the equation $y=x^3-\dfrac14x^4$. Find all intercepts.
questions.answer: $y$-intercept: $x=0\Rightarrow y=0$. $x$-intercepts: $x^3\left(1-\tfrac14x\right)=0\Rightarrow x=0$ or $x=4$. The intercepts are $(0,0)$ and $(4,0)$.

questions.question: A curve has the equation $y=x^3-\dfrac14x^4$. Find the stationary points and determine their nature.
questions.answer:
$y'=3x^2-x^3=x^2(3-x)=0\Rightarrow x=0$ or $x=3$.

$y(0)=0$ and $y(3)=27-\tfrac{81}4=\tfrac{27}4=6.75$.

$y''=6x-3x^2$. At $x=3$: $y''=18-27=-9<0$, so $(3,6.75)$ is a **local maximum**.

At $x=0$: $y''=0$, so test the sign of $y'$: $y'(-1)=3+1=4>0$ and $y'(1)=3-1=2>0$. The gradient is positive on both sides, so $(0,0)$ is a **horizontal point of inflexion** (stationary, not a turning point).

questions.question: A curve has the equation $y=x^3-\dfrac14x^4$. Find any points of inflexion.
questions.answer:
$y''=6x-3x^2=3x(2-x)=0\Rightarrow x=0$ or $x=2$.

Check the concavity changes: $y''(-1)=-9<0$, $y''(1)=3>0$, $y''(3)=-9<0$, so $y''$ changes sign at both $x=0$ and $x=2$.

$y(2)=8-4=4$. The points of inflexion are $(0,0)$ and $(2,4)$.

questions.question: A curve has the equation $y=x^3-\dfrac14x^4$, with intercepts $(0,0)$ and $(4,0)$, a maximum at $(3,6.75)$, and inflexions at $(0,0)$ (horizontal) and $(2,4)$. Hence sketch the graph, indicating all key features.
questions.answer: The graph has a horizontal point of inflexion at the origin (it passes through the origin tangent to the $x$-axis, rising), an inflexion at $(2,4)$, a local maximum at $(3,6.75)$ and crosses the $x$-axis again at $(4,0)$. For $x<0$ the graph is below the axis, and as $x\to\pm\infty$, $y\to-\infty$ (the leading term is $-\tfrac14x^4$).

questions.question: Differentiate $y=3x\sin x$.
questions.answer: Product rule: $y'=3\sin x+3x\cos x$.

questions.question: Given that $\dfrac{d}{dx}(3x\sin x)=3\sin x+3x\cos x$, hence find $\displaystyle\int3x\cos x\,dx$.
questions.answer:
Integrating both sides of $\frac{d}{dx}(3x\sin x)=3x\cos x+3\sin x$:
$$3x\sin x=\int3x\cos x\,dx+\int3\sin x\,dx\Rightarrow\int3x\cos x\,dx=3x\sin x-\int3\sin x\,dx=3x\sin x+3\cos x+C.$$

questions.question:
The lifetime, $X$ hours, of a battery has a cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ given by
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0&x<10\\ \dfrac1{128}\left(x^2-12x+20\right)&10\le x\le18\\ 1&x>18\end{cases}$$
The lifetime of a battery is guaranteed to be at least 10 hours but never more than 18 hours. Sketch the cumulative distribution function.
questions.answer: $F(x)=0$ for $x<10$; on $10\le x\le18$ the graph is an increasing parabola from $F(10)=\frac{100-120+20}{128}=0$ to $F(18)=\frac{324-216+20}{128}=1$; and $F(x)=1$ for $x>18$. The graph is continuous, non-decreasing, and takes values between 0 and 1.

questions.question: The lifetime, $X$ hours, of a battery has a cumulative distribution function $F(x)=\dfrac1{128}\left(x^2-12x+20\right)$ for $10\le x\le18$ ($F=0$ for $x<10$, $F=1$ for $x>18$). An outdoor lantern requires three batteries, all of which must be working, to operate. Three new batteries are inserted into the lantern. Find the probability that the lantern will still be working after 15 hours. Give your answer as a decimal, rounded to three decimal places. (Assume the batteries fail independently.)
questions.answer:
For one battery: $P(X>15)=1-F(15)=1-\dfrac{225-180+20}{128}=1-\dfrac{65}{128}=\dfrac{63}{128}$.

All three must still be working (independent): $\left(\dfrac{63}{128}\right)^3=0.119$ (3 d.p.).

questions.question: The lifetime, $X$ hours, of a battery has a cumulative distribution function $F(x)=\dfrac1{128}\left(x^2-12x+20\right)$ for $10\le x\le18$ ($F=0$ for $x<10$, $F=1$ for $x>18$). Find the probability density function of the random variable $X$.
questions.answer: $f(x)=F'(x)=\dfrac1{128}(2x-12)=\dfrac{x-6}{64}$ for $10\le x\le18$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise.

questions.question: A particle moves along the $x$-axis, and after $t$ seconds its velocity, in metres per second, is given by $v=\dfrac{5\pi}3\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}3\right)$. Initially, the particle is 3 metres to the right of the origin. Find an equation for the displacement of the particle.
questions.answer:
$$x=\int\frac{5\pi}3\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}3\right)dt=\frac{5\pi}3\cdot\frac3\pi\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}3\right)+C=5\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}3\right)+C.$$
At $t=0$, $x=3$: $3=5\sin0+C\Rightarrow C=3$.
$$x=5\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}3\right)+3.$$

questions.question: A particle moves along the $x$-axis with velocity $v=\dfrac{5\pi}3\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}3\right)$ m/s and displacement $x=5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}3\right)+3$ m. Find when the particle is at rest for the second time and hence find the total distance travelled at this time.
questions.answer:
At rest: $v=0\Rightarrow\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}3\right)=0\Rightarrow\frac{\pi t}3=\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2,\ldots\Rightarrow t=\frac32,\ \frac92,\ \ldots$ The second time is $t=\dfrac92$ s.

Positions: $x(0)=3$; $x\left(\tfrac32\right)=5\sin\frac\pi2+3=8$; $x\left(\tfrac92\right)=5\sin\frac{3\pi}2+3=-2$.

The particle moves from $3$ to $8$ (5 m), then turns and moves from $8$ to $-2$ (10 m). Total distance $=5+10=15$ m.

questions.question: A particle moves along the $x$-axis with velocity $v=\dfrac{5\pi}3\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}3\right)$ m/s. Find the exact acceleration of the particle when $t=0.5$.
questions.answer:
$a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-\dfrac{5\pi}3\cdot\dfrac\pi3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}3\right)=-\dfrac{5\pi^2}9\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}3\right)$.

At $t=0.5$: $a=-\dfrac{5\pi^2}9\sin\dfrac\pi6=-\dfrac{5\pi^2}9\cdot\dfrac12=-\dfrac{5\pi^2}{18}$ m/s$^2$.

questions.question: Below is a map of a local parkland. The curved boundary of the parkland has equation $y=-\dfrac{27}{80}x^4+2x$ (distances in km). Meg, the park developer, wants to build a golf course in the shape of a right-angled triangle, with one vertex at the origin, base along the $x$-axis of length $g$ kilometres, and the third vertex on the curve above $x=g$. Show that the area of the proposed golf course is $A=-\dfrac{27}{160}g^5+g^2$.
questions.answer:
The base is $g$ and the height is the $y$-value of the curve at $x=g$: $h=-\dfrac{27}{80}g^4+2g$.
$$A=\tfrac12\times g\times\left(-\frac{27}{80}g^4+2g\right)=-\frac{27}{160}g^5+g^2.$$

questions.question: A golf course is a right-angled triangle with base $g$ km along the $x$-axis and area $A=-\dfrac{27}{160}g^5+g^2$ (the third vertex lies on the curve $y=-\dfrac{27}{80}x^4+2x$, with $g>0$). Find the maximum area of the golf course, clearly showing that it is a maximum.
questions.answer:
$A'=-\dfrac{135}{160}g^4+2g=g\left(2-\dfrac{27}{32}g^3\right)=0\Rightarrow g=0$ (rejected) or $g^3=\dfrac{64}{27}\Rightarrow g=\dfrac43$.

$A''=-\dfrac{540}{160}g^3+2=-\dfrac{27}8g^3+2$. At $g=\frac43$: $A''=-\frac{27}8\cdot\frac{64}{27}+2=-8+2=-6<0$, so this is a maximum.

$$A_{max}=-\frac{27}{160}\left(\frac43\right)^5+\left(\frac43\right)^2=-\frac{27}{160}\cdot\frac{1024}{243}+\frac{16}9=-\frac{32}{45}+\frac{80}{45}=\frac{48}{45}=\frac{16}{15}\text{ km}^2\ (\approx1.067\text{ km}^2).$$

questions.question: Steve borrows \$40 000 at a rate of 4.8% p.a., compounded monthly. At the end of each month, he makes a repayment of \$$M$. Let $A_n$ be the amount owing after $n$ months. By building an expression, show that $A_3=40\,000(1.004)^3-M\left(1+1.004+1.004^2\right)$.

Steve borrows \$40 000 at a rate of 4.8% p.a., compounded monthly (so $0.4\%$ per month). At the end of each month, he makes a repayment of \$$M$. After 4 years, Steve doubles the monthly repayment. He pays off the loan in full at the end of 8 years in total. Find the value of $M$.
questions.answer:
Let $A_n$ be the balance after $n$ months. After 48 months (4 years), then with repayment $2M$ for the next 48 months:
$$A_{96}=40\,000(1.004)^{96}-M\left(1.004^{95}+1.004^{94}+\cdots+1.004^{48}\right)-2M\left(1.004^{47}+\cdots+1.004+1\right)=0.$$
(The first 48 payments of $M$ are each compounded for $95,\ldots,48$ months and the last 48 payments of $2M$ for $47,\ldots,0$ months.)

Geometric series with $r=1.004$ and 48 terms:

$1.004^{48}+\cdots+1.004^{95}=1.004^{48}\cdot\dfrac{1.004^{48}-1}{0.004}=63.95\ldots$

$1+1.004+\cdots+1.004^{47}=\dfrac{1.004^{48}-1}{0.004}=52.80\ldots$ so the $2M$ term contributes $2\times52.80=105.60\ldots$

$$M(63.95+105.60)=40\,000(1.004)^{96}\Rightarrow M=\frac{40\,000(1.004)^{96}}{169.55\ldots}=\$346.08.$$
